items.abstract:
<jats:p>  	Hydrogen is regarded as the most promising energy carrier. The pure hydrogen produced from electrochemical water splitting by using renewable energy is the most attractive and effective approach.[1] In comparison to alkaline water electrolysis, proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) could operate at higher current densities, lower ohmic loss, more compact system design, faster system response and more stable towards load-cycling and shutdowns. [2] The sluggish kinetics of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at the anode of PEMWEs has restricted its practical applications. To date, iridium (Ir) metal and its oxide are usually selected as the state-of-the-art catalyst for OER due to their robust and long-term durability under the harsh acidic conditions. Nevertheless, Ir is an extremely scarce element, and its price has been doubled in the past few years. The development of low cost and highly effective electrocatalyst for OER in an acidic medium is urgently needed but remains a great challenge.</jats:p>
               <jats:p>In this work, we have prepared an ultra-thin RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> nanosheets by a simple molten salt method. High resolution STEM results show that the as-prepared RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> nanosheets is about 1-2 nm in thickness and hold a large number of defects, like Ru vacancy, grain boundary and amorphous. Toward OER, the as-prepared RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> nanosheets demonstrate an outstanding OER activity in acidic electrolyte, with an overpotential of only 199 mV for reach the current density of 10 mA cm<jats:sup>-2</jats:sup>
                  <jats:sub>geo</jats:sub> at a catalyst loading of 125 μg cm<jats:sup>-2</jats:sup>
                  <jats:sub>geo</jats:sub>. At the overpotential of 230 mV, the specific and mass activities of RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> nanosheets electrode is up to 0.89 mA cm<jats:sup>-2</jats:sup>
                  <jats:sub>oxide</jats:sub> and 0.516 A mg<jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>
                  <jats:sub>Ru</jats:sub>, which is 14.9 and 80.5 times higher than that of commercial RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                  <jats:sub> </jats:sub>catalyst, respectively. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations (Figure 2e and 2f) indicated that the Ru vacancy defect on RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> surface could servers as the highly active site for remarkably weaken the binding energies of *O as compared to that of *OOH, which decrease the energy gap between ΔG<jats:sub>O</jats:sub> and ΔG<jats:sub>OOH</jats:sub> and thus dramatic enhanced OER performance. We also applied the catalysts in a homemade PEMWE device, at the applied cell voltage of 1.65 V, the current density of the RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> nanosheets catalyst cell reaches 0.93 A cm<jats:sup>-2</jats:sup>, which is almost 3 times larger than that of the cell with commercial RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> catalyst (0.31 A cm<jats:sup>-2</jats:sup>) at the same conditions, demonstrating that the RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> nanosheets possess great potential toward developing high performance PEMWEs.</jats:p>
               <jats:p>This work is under progress. Meanwhile, further characterizations, including XRD, XPS and more detailed morphology and electrochemical performance characterization of the RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> nanosheets catalyst will be presented at the meeting.</jats:p>
               <jats:p>The work described in this paper was financially supported by the Shenzhen Clean Energy Research Institute (No. CERI-KY-2019-003), Shenzhen Peacock Plan (KQTD2016022620054656), Shenzhen Key Laboratory project (ZDSYS201603311013489), The authors acknowledge the assistance of SUSTech Core Research Facilities.</jats:p>
               <jats:p>References</jats:p>
               <jats:p>1. Shi, Q.; Zhu, C.; Du, D.; Lin, Y., Robust noble metal-based electrocatalysts for oxygen evolution reaction. Chem Soc Rev 2019, 48 (12), 3181-3192.</jats:p>
               <jats:p>2. Kibsgaard, J.; Chorkendorff, I., Considerations for the scaling-up of water splitting catalysts. Nature Energy 2019, 4 (6), 430-433.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Supported metal catalysts with appropriate metal‐support interactions (MSIs) hold a great promise for heterogeneous catalysis. However, ensuring tight immobilization of metal clusters/nanoparticles on the support while maximizing the exposure of surface active sites remains a huge challenge. Herein, we report an Ir/WO<jats:sub>3</jats:sub> catalyst with a new enrooted‐type MSI in which Ir clusters are, unprecedentedly, atomically enrooted into the WO<jats:sub>3</jats:sub> lattice. The enrooted Ir atoms decrease the electron density of the constructed interface compared to the adhered (root‐free) type, thereby achieving appropriate adsorption toward oxygen intermediates, ultimately leading to high activity and stability for oxygen evolution in acidic media. Importantly, this work provides a new enrooted‐type supported metal catalyst, which endows suitable MSI and maximizes the exposure of surface active sites in contrast to the conventional adhered, embedded, and encapsulated types.</jats:p>
title: Enrooted‐Type Metal‐Support Interaction Boosting Oxygen Evolution Reaction in Acidic Media
